skill.name: weekly-report
skill.description: Guides users through creating clear weekly work reports from scattered work notes, outcomes, blockers, and next steps.
skill.summary: Create structured weekly reports that show work value, limits, and next actions.
skill.author: yunshu0909

content.value_statement: Weekly reports are hard when work details are scattered. This skill guides collection, structure, and revision so users can produce clear updates.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through collecting weekly work details by module and role.
Organizes work into sections for engineering, product, operations, design, QA, sales, and general roles.
Prompts for background, actions, results, status, blockers, owners, and next steps.
Drafts a structured weekly report with current work and next week priorities.
Helps revise tone, structure, and emphasis while preserving the user's writing style.
limitations: It does not verify the factual accuracy of user-provided work details.
It does not collect data from project trackers or external systems by itself.
It may need user review to match company-specific report formats.
It cannot infer important context that the user does not provide.

use_cases.title: Summarize engineering work
use_cases.description: Turn completed features, bug fixes, reviews, blockers, and next steps into a clear weekly engineering update.

use_cases.title: Prepare product and operations updates
use_cases.description: Organize research, launches, data analysis, user feedback, and follow-up actions into a structured weekly report.

use_cases.title: Create team status reports
use_cases.description: Convert scattered team notes into a concise report that shows progress, risks, owners, and next week priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Draft my weekly report
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write this week's report. Ask what I worked on, then organize it into a clear draft.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for starting from a blank page.

prompt_templates.title: Organize scattered notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are my rough notes: [paste notes]. Group them by work area, identify missing details, and ask concise follow-up questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the user has notes but no structure.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this weekly report draft. Keep my tone, strengthen the logic, add provided metrics, and clarify blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a draft already exists.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a manager-ready update
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit my weekly report for my manager. Use these tasks, risks, and next actions. Keep it concise and do not exaggerate.

output_examples.input: I fixed checkout bugs, reviewed pull requests, and started payment logging.
output_examples.output: A draft groups the work into bug fixes, code review, and observability, with status and next steps for each item.

output_examples.input: My notes are messy and I do not know what mattered.
output_examples.output: The skill asks follow-up questions about impact, blockers, owners, and next week priorities before drafting the report.

output_examples.input: I need a customer delivery update for this week.
output_examples.output: A concise report covers customer work, delivery status, open risks, and agreed next actions.

best_practices: Provide rough notes first, then answer follow-up questions about impact and status.
Include numbers, customer feedback, or delivery dates when they are available.
Review the final draft for company terminology, sensitive details, and factual accuracy.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to exaggerate outcomes or hide unresolved blockers.
Do not paste confidential customer or company data unless your environment allows it.
Do not accept the final report without checking facts, owners, and next steps.

faq.question: Does this skill write the report from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start from a blank page by asking questions about your weekly work.

faq.question: Can it work with messy notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can group rough notes, identify missing details, and create a structured draft.

faq.question: Does it support different job roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for engineering, product, operations, design, QA, sales, and general work.

faq.question: Will it invent metrics or results?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for measurable details but should not create numbers the user did not provide.

faq.question: Can it preserve my writing style?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow asks the assistant to keep the user's expression and adjust only where needed.

faq.question: Does it connect to Jira, GitHub, or documents?
faq.answer: No. It relies on information provided in the conversation unless other tools are separately available.
